# Interface Releases

> Signed release manifests for the gibs.finance interface, and a free,
> self-hostable backend for its cross-chain quote aggregation. This
> repository carries no application source code — it exists so a public
> place can hold release artifacts and self-hosting instructions for a
> project whose source repository stays private.

## What a release is

Every publish of the gibs.finance interface creates one GitHub Release
here, tagged `<version>+<7-character commit>` (for example
`1.13.1+e4f5a6b`), carrying three files:

- `interface-<id>.car` — a Content Archive of that release's built
  interface, packed for the InterPlanetary File System with Content ID
  version 1 and raw leaves.
- `version.json` — the signed manifest this release updated the default
  branch to.
- `version.json.sig` — a detached Ed25519 signature over the exact bytes
  of that `version.json`.

The current manifest also lives at this repository's default branch, as
`version.json` and `version.json.sig`, alongside `public-keys.json` — the
Ed25519 public key registry used to verify it.

## How to verify a release

1. Fetch `version.json` and `version.json.sig` — either this
   repository's default branch, or a specific release's own assets.
2. Fetch `public-keys.json` and find the entry whose key matches the
   `keyId` named in `version.json.sig`.
3. Verify the Ed25519 signature in `version.json.sig` over the exact
   bytes of `version.json`, using that public key.
4. Read the release you want out of `version.json`'s `releases` array (or
   `channels`/`latest`) to get its Content ID (`cid`).
5. Fetch the content from any InterPlanetary File System gateway using
   that Content ID — for example
   `https://<cid>.ipfs.4everland.io/`.

## The public key

`public-keys.json`, on this repository's default branch, is the source
of truth for every key that has ever signed a `version.json` here:

```json
{
  "<keyId>": {
    "publicKeyBase64": "<32 raw bytes, base64>",
    "algorithm": "Ed25519",
    "createdAt": "<ISO 8601 timestamp>"
  }
}
```

An entry is never removed while any reachable release still carries a
signature made with it — key rotation adds a new entry alongside the
old one rather than replacing it, so every past release stays
verifiable.

## Run your own backend

The gibs.finance interface works entirely on its own, calling LI.FI,
Relay, and NEAR Intents directly from the browser. It also supports an
optional backend, `@gibs/quote-service`, that fans the same requests out
to those three providers and shares one upstream call between every
visitor asking the same question — no provider key required to start.
Point your own build of the interface at your own instance instead of
the gibs.finance one, or run one for any other reason.

See [`self-host/README.md`](self-host/README.md) for the full guide, and
its "Image availability" notice for the current state of the published
container image. See [`skills/integrate-gibs-quotes/SKILL.md`](skills/integrate-gibs-quotes/SKILL.md)
for a task-oriented walkthrough: choosing a mode, installing the
`@gibs/quotes` client package, and wiring it to a self-hosted or direct
configuration.
